messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for service/api-gateway (commit abc123) detected elevated 500s on canary cohort, 3/5 hosts failing, started 2026-03-15T09:12:30Z :rotating_light:
olivia: paging oncall — I'm taking this. seeing 500 spikes in graphs. canary started ~09:10. tagging here so infra can jump in @sam @kai
sam: on it. pulling canary logs now. are these internal errors or upstream timeout?
kai: adding context: deploy used image tag service-api:2026-03-15-abc123 from registry.us-east.redwood.io. canary nodes show OOMs in kube events then 500s.
olivia: quick customer impact check — Matt can you confirm if any customer reports?
matt: getting one support thread — a customer reported 502s at 09:14, low volume. looks like some requests get routed to canary only. estimate: ~0.6% of total traffic affected so far.
anna: paging in SRE. quick triage: grabbing artifact digest from registry and comparing to build artifacts. suspicious retagging patterns have come up in past incidents.
sam: registry query shows tag service-api:2026-03-15-abc123 resolves to digest sha256:deadbeef... but CI artifact metadata for that commit expected sha256:feedface... mismatch. possible retag or cache poison during push.
olivia: ok that's actionable. put kill-switch on canary rollout and stop traffic to canary nodes. kai can you run the rollout abort?
kai: aborting canary via kubectl and our rollout tool now. running commands:
```
rolloutctl abort api-gateway --canary
kubectl scale deploy api-gateway-canary --replicas=0 -n prod
```
(kubectl returned 200)
deploy-bot: Canary abort acknowledged. scaling canary to 0.
sam: next, preventing further bad images: revoking tag binding for service-api:2026-03-15-abc123 in registry and pinning traffic to previous tag. running registry lock script.
anna: to be safe, flip feature flag FEA_CANARY_V2 to off for prod: `flagsctl set FEA_CANARY_V2 false --env=prod`
olivia: done, flag off confirmed. routing now back to stable.
matt: customers: support notified of mitigation. advising engineers to expect a follow-up email. severity P2 for now due to partial impact and quick rollback.
sam: root cause hypothesis: CI publish step had a transient mirror issue that led to tag pointing to wrong digest (cache poisoning/retag). CI job logs show a retry path that doesn't validate digest on subsequent pushes. attaching log snippet:
```
[CI] push service-api:2026-03-15-abc123 -> registry mirror.us-east (200)
[CI] push service-api:2026-03-15-abc123 -> registry.us-east (retry)
[CI] push complete (no digest validation on retry)
```

olivia: action items for immediate mitigations: 1) registry tag lock for this repo 2) fail CI on any push where digest != artifact metadata 3) postmortem and customer comms draft. sam/anna, can you own 1 & 2?
sam: I'll open a registry incident and implement tag-lock rule. ETA 2 hours for initial lock + smoke tests.
anna: I'll add digest validation to CI pipeline + a quick guard that fails the job on mismatch. ETA 3 hours to rollout to all pipelines.
kai: oncall handoff in 40min — I'll create a short runbook for night oncall in case recurrence happens.
olivia: thanks. incident-bot: creating incident ticket with severity P2, linkage to support thread, and ops runbook.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-07 created, owner: olivia, severity: P2, playbook: canary-abort-retag
olivia: closing paging for immediate mitigation — system health returning to baseline, 500s back to normal in graphs. leaving incident open for follow-up and root cause. good work everyone :thumbsup:
matt: I'll draft the customer note and ping legal/security if we determine any credential issues.
sam: log pointers and initial diffs saved under /var/logs/incidents/INC-2026-0315-07. will follow up in a separate thread for the postmortem.
olivia: thanks team. I'll update incident ticket with timeline and mark follow-ups. moving to postmortem prep.
